summary: A 1935 ground-level lookout in the Angeles National Forest, burned in the 2009 Station Fire and rebuilt in 2019-2020 by ANFFLA and Southern California Edison, now staffed again by volunteers.

facts.design: 14x14 ft ground-level ('C3') cab with steel shutters; rebuilt 2019-2020 in concrete board and steel framing

access.note: Popular day-hike destination off Angeles Crest Highway; open to visitors

visit.trail_note: Easy hike from the Chilao-Charlton Flats area; cab sits on the ground, accessible to visitors with limited mobility

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service - Angeles National Forest

events.note: NHLR gives 1935; ANFFLA's own tower-data table also gives 'Date Built: 1935' although the ANFFLA narrative text elsewhere says 1937
Reopened to the public by ANFFLA volunteers May 30, 1998; registered on NHLR October 1, 1998
Destroyed by the Station Fire, September 1, 2009
Reconstruction with Southern California Edison began September 18, 2019
Rebuild completed April 2020; first staffed again over July 4th weekend 2020

evidence.supports: built 1935, 14x14 ground house with steel shutters
evidence.quote: The 14' x 14' C3 ground house is equipped with steel shutters as protection against vandals.

evidence.supports: one of only two lookouts remaining on Angeles NF of 19
evidence.quote: One of only two lookouts remaining on the Angeles National Forest out of a network that once numbered 19

evidence.supports: friendliest lookout, accessible to visitors with limited mobility
evidence.quote: The 14 x 14 foot wooden cab with its high ceiling has been called the “friendliest lookout” because it sits directly on the ground and is accessible to visitors with limited mobility.
the Vetter Mountain Lookout was re-opened to the public by volunteers on May 30, 1998.
Vetter Lookout was lost in the Station Fire, September 1, 2009.

evidence.supports: destroyed by Station Fire August 2009 (month given as August by ANFFLA, versus September 1 per NHLR)
evidence.quote: The original tower was destroyed by the Station Fire in August of 2009.

evidence.supports: rebuild via SCE partnership began September 18 2019
evidence.quote: Vetter Mountain Lookout, through a partnership with Southern California Edison, began reconstruction on September 18, 2019 - 10 years after the loss of the original structure.

evidence.supports: rebuild completed April 2020, reopened July 4th weekend 2020
evidence.quote: Construction of the rebuilt Vetter Mountain Lookout was completed April, 2020 and reopened for service July 4th weekend, 2020.

evidence.supports: rebuilt lookout made of concrete board and steel frames
evidence.quote: The rebuilt Vetter Lookout is made of concrete board and steel frames.

evidence.supports: about 60 trained volunteers staff it, sunrise to sunset, 1-3 at a time
evidence.quote: About 60 trained volunteers help staff the Vetter Mountain Fire Lookout located at the top of the San Gabriel Mountains. From sunrise to sunset, one to three volunteers hike up to watch for possible smoke and fire in the area, helping to alert forest rangers.
The Osborne Fire Finder helps measure the distance of visible smoke or fire in the area.

evidence.supports: ANFFLA volunteers kept watch from a temporary structure for 10 years between the 2009 fire and the 2019-2020 rebuild
evidence.quote: For 10 years ANFFLA volunteers continued to maintain fire lookout services at Vetter Mountain with a temporary structure.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR and ANFFLA's own data table both say 1935, but ANFFLA's narrative paragraph separately says 'Originally built in 1937'. Treated 1935 as correct since it is corroborated twice (NHLR, and ANFFLA's own tower-data field), while 1937 appears only once in prose on the same page.

NHLR dates the Station Fire loss to September 1, 2009; ANFFLA's narrative says 'August of 2009'. The Station Fire itself is widely documented as starting August 26 and burning through early September 2009, so both are plausible depending on when Vetter specifically was lost; story uses NHLR's more specific date.

notes_for_editor: Two minor date conflicts (build year 1935 vs 1937, and burn month August vs September 2009) are noted in resolved_conflicts; both resolved toward the more corroborated/specific NHLR figures. Did not verify current-day staffing schedule beyond the 2023-era Edison article, which may be slightly dated.
